title: Multi-Dimensional SLO Reconciliation and Emergency Capacity Playbook
author: Leah Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a pragmatic, multi-dimensional approach to reconciling SLO consumption across latency, availability, and cost dimensions and executing emergency capacity interventions when SLOs are at risk. It consolidates detection thresholds, containment actions, capacity allocation heuristics, automation recipes, and post-incident evidence requirements into a single reference for on-call SREs and service owners.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-containment for SLO breaches to under 15 minutes for P0 events.
- Provide predictable, auditable steps for temporary capacity allocation and rollback.
- Ensure every emergency capacity change is linked to reproducible telemetry and a post-incident remediation plan.

Scope
- Applies to all multi-tenant model serving surfaces (text-gen, chat, embeddings) and routing layers where SLOs are defined.
- Covers incidents driven by load, degraded kernel performance (OOM, NVLink errors), network region failure, or model-serving regressions.
- Excludes scheduled capacity provisioning (handled by capacity PLANNING runbooks) and non-SLO business metrics.

Key Definitions
- SLO vector: A tuple of {availability, p95 latency, error rate} used to evaluate service health.
- Burn window: Time-series window used for burn-rate calculation (default 5m / 1h).
- Emergency capacity: Short-lived pool (hours) of reserved GPU/CPU that can be attached to a tenant or route.
- Safe-mode: A traffic shaping state (reduced concurrency, degraded feature gates) used prior to heavy capacity changes.

Governance and Ownership (table)
| Area | Primary owner | Escalation | Notes |
| Service SLO definition | Service owner (product or platform) | SRE on-call | Verify SLO vector correctness before intervention |
| Emergency capacity allocation | SRE on-call lead | Head of infra | Requires ticket for >8h allocation |
| Automation / scripts | Runbook author | Infra eng | PR + staged rollout required |
| Postmortem & remediation | Incident commander | Service owner | Must include capacity cost estimate |

Thresholds and Triggers (summary)
- Warning: 5% burn rate sustained for 30m or p95 latency > SLO + 25% for 10m.
- Actionable: 15% burn rate sustained for 5m or error rate above SLO threshold for 5m.
- Critical: 50% burn rate over the configured SLO window, or p95 > SLO * 2 for >5m.

Detection -> Initial Triage (steps)
1) Alert fired: SLO-observability alerts target the service Slack channel and PagerDuty.
2) Triage checklist (first 5 minutes):
   a. Confirm alert validity: check synthetic canary / health-check endpoints.
   b. Check model variants and recent rollouts (Console > Rollouts).
   c. Identify scope: single region, single model, or cross-region.
   d. Snapshot key telemetry (p95, p99, qps, queue_length, cpu/gpu_util, free_mem, kvcache hit-rate).
3) Set status: if actionable/critical, declare incident and assign IC.

Containment Patterns (pick based on cause)
- Hot-tenant overload: apply token-priority rate limit for offending tenant + enable per-tenant priority queue.
- Kernel/oom cascade: drain affected nodes, set serving pool to safe-mode concurrency=1, and divert traffic to standby pool.
- Model regression: auto-fallback to last-known-good model variant for affected routes.
- Region outage: initiate regional failover routing policy and warm standby in secondary region.

Emergency Capacity Allocation Procedure (step-by-step)
1) Confirm need (IC): attach last 30 minutes of burn metrics and a short justification in incident doc.
2) Select allocation mode:
   a. Hot add (fast): attach emergency GPU instances from reservoir (recommended for <2h).
   b. Spillover (safe): route a subset of traffic to a pre-warmed burst cluster with reduced QoS.
   c. Tenant throttle + burst (economical): prioritize critical tenants and allocate emergency slices.
3) Execute allocation: run the approved infra CLI command (example below).
4) Validate: confirm p95 latency and queue length return toward normal within 10 minutes.
5) Record allocation: create capacity change ticket with duration and cost estimate.

Example CLI (Infrastructure)
- Attach emergency pool (fast):
  rwinfra attach-pool --pool emergency-reservoir --service service-name --gpus 4 --duration 2h --reason "SLO emergency: high burn"

Safe-mode and Traffic Shaping (JSON policy sample)
{
  "policy_name": "safe-mode-default",
  "concurrency": 1,
  "rate_limit_per_tenant": 20,
  "feature_gates": {"contextual_reranking": false, "prefetch_kvcache": false},
  "fallback_model": "service-name:model:v1-stable"
}

Capacity Allocation YAML (example)
allocation_policy:
  name: emergency-shard-attach
  max_gpus: 8
  prewarm: true
  rollback_window_minutes: 30
  notify: ["sre-oncall", "service-owner"]

Validation and Rollback Criteria
- Validation: p95 decreases by at least 20% of the observed delta and queue_length drops by 50% within 10 minutes of allocation.
- If validation fails after two allocation attempts, escalate to Head of Infra for cross-cluster migration.
- Automatic rollback: allocations with duration <= 2h will auto-expire. Manual rollback required for allocations >2h.

Communication Templates
- Pager update (short): "Investigating SLO breach for service-name. Applying emergency capacity (4 GPUs). Expected impact: reduced p95 in 8-12 mins. IC: @name."
- Customer-facing status: "We are experiencing elevated latency for model previews in region X. We are applying mitigations and expect restoration within 30 minutes."

Telemetry & Evidence Requirements (must capture and attach)
- Time-series snapshots: p95, p50, p99, qps, queue length, gpu_util, node_free_mem, kvcache_hit_rate at 1m granularity for the incident window.
- Traces: representative slow traces (sampled) for 5 requests per minute during the incident.
- Correlating events: deployment IDs, model variants, infra attach/detach logs.
- Cost estimate: estimated additional GPU-hours and projected dollar cost.

Post-Incident Work and Remediation (mandatory within 7 days)
1) Evidence bundle: attach collected telemetry and CLI history to postmortem.
2) Root cause analysis: include why the SLO vector moved and why the first containment failed or succeeded.
3) Remediation plan: sizing changes, autoscale tuning, model rollbacks, and engineering tickets.
4) Capacity reconciliation: ensure emergency allocations are reconciled with invoicing and resource ledger.
5) Follow-up action: capacity-harden, add synthetic canaries, or increase reservoir for the tenant.

Playbook Automation Recipes (examples)
- Auto-attach policy (pseudocode):
  if burn_rate > 0.15 for 5m and kvcache_hit_rate < 0.6:
    trigger attach-pool --pool emergency-reservoir --gpus 2 --duration 1h --tag auto-attach
  else if p95_latency > slo*1.5:
    disable non-critical feature_gates and notify oncall

Testing and Rehearsal Cadence
- Monthly tabletop on-call drills using anonymized synthetic workloads.
- Quarterly dry-run: simulate emergency attach with canary traffic to validate automation and rollback.
- Pre-launch: every major model onboarding must pass a capacity-rehearsal checklist (see related pages).

Safety and Cost Controls
- Guardrails: automated cost cap at $X/day for emergency allocations per team (configured in infra).
- Approval: allocations > $Y or >8h require written approval from Head of Infra.
- Auditing: all emergency actions are logged and audited weekly by SRE compliance.

Appendix A — Minimal Incident Checklist (quick reference)
1) Confirm alert and set P1/P2/P3 classification.
2) Snapshot telemetry and assign IC.
3) Apply containment (safe-mode / rate limit / model fallback).
4) If containment insufficient, attach emergency capacity (document justification).
5) Validate and monitor for 30m.
6) Start post-incident evidence collection and ticketing.
